card.summary: Free: 1:1 real-time transfer up to 50 GB; LINK creation capped at 10 GB. Lite $5.99/mo raises download data to 200 GB.

free_tier.stated: Free: 1:1 real-time transfer up to 50 GB; LINK creation capped at 10 GB. Lite $5.99/mo raises download data to 200 GB.

egress.terms: download-data metered on the recipient side (that is what the paid 'Download data' allowance buys).

record.tooling: The Open API Service was RETIRED — support article 'End of support for Open API Service (26.3.31)'. No SDK path remains.
record.chaining: The 50 GB figure is real-time device-to-device, not stored. Stored links are 10 GB and die on expiry with no recovery ('all files are deleted from the server once a link expires').
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: 10 GB stored link / 50 GB real-time. Retention: expires, and expired links are unrecoverable. pull-count: 'download data' is a metered allowance. This is the actual binding constraint on free, and exhausting it blocks further downloads from your own links.
record.reliability_note: Dead API and metered read path.

evidence.proved: Free: '1:1 real-time file transfer up to 50GB', 'Link creation up to 10GB'
'all files are deleted from the server once a link expires. After this point, they cannot be retrieved'
policy change moving free users to a link-download allowance
